author: Owen Lin
date: "2026-09-23"
---

Setting up my environment:

```{python}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#setup
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

Loading in relevant data:
```{python}
#loading in data and pulling columns we need

penguins = load_penguins()
penguins[["species", "year", "body_mass_g"]].head()
```

Calculating the average body mass by year for each species:

```{python}
#Average body mass by year and species

avg_mass_by_year = penguins.groupby(["year", "species"])["body_mass_g"].mean().unstack()

avg_mass_by_year
```

Plotting our results:
```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-mass-by-year-and-species
#| fig-cap: "Body mass of penguins by year and species."
ax = avg_mass_by_year.plot(marker="o")
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("Average body mass (g)")
ax.set_xticks(avg_mass_by_year.index)
plt.show()
```

Our results show that Gentoo penguins are clearly the heaviest species and that the average mass per species has been relatively stable over the three years in the data set.
